---
title: "Chapter 2: Measuring Uncertainty"
subtitle: "Entropy, cross-entropy, and KL divergence — the math behind every language model's loss function."
---

How do you measure whether predictions are any good? Claude Shannon answered this in 1948. This chapter builds his idea from scratch — first on a toy game, then on real data.

## Chapter Materials

- [Lesson](lesson.md) — written walkthrough with references
- [Notebook](notebook.ipynb) — runnable exercises
- [Video](video.qmd) — recordings

## Readings

### Easy

**Information Theory & Entropy**

- [Visual Information Theory](https://colah.github.io/posts/2015-09-Visual-Information/) by Chris Olah — Beautiful visual explanation of entropy, mutual information, and KL divergence

**Compression Algorithms**

- [Huffman Coding](https://go-compression.github.io/algorithms/huffman/) — How variable-length codes achieve near-optimal compression using entropy
- [Arithmetic Coding](https://go-compression.github.io/algorithms/arithmetic/) — A more sophisticated approach that can achieve compression arbitrarily close to the entropy limit

**N-grams & Language Models**

- [Chapter 3: N-gram Language Models](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/3.pdf) from Speech and Language Processing by Jurafsky & Martin — The classic textbook chapter on n-grams and perplexity

### Advanced

**Information Theory Foundations**

- [A Mathematical Theory of Communication](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~ctm/home/text/others/shannon/entropy/entropy.pdf) by Claude Shannon (1948) — The original paper that started it all (Sections I-II are most relevant)
